paper.title: LM-Nav: Robotic Navigation with Large Pre-Trained Models of Language, Vision, and Action
paper.central_claim: LM-Nav composes large pretrained language, vision and navigation models without target-environment finetuning or language-labelled navigation data, allowing a mobile robot to follow free-form textual instructions over long distances in novel outdoor settings.
paper.central_claim_son55_wording: A navigation system assembled only from frozen pre-trained models (GPT-3 landmark extraction, CLIP grounding on a topological graph, ViNG navigation model, graph search over a joint likelihood) follows free-form outdoor instructions on a real wheeled robot without fine-tuning or language-annotated robot data; 85% of 20 queries (over 6 km) succeeded.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Closed-loop real-robot traversals with counts (20 single runs); the topological graph is built from manual driving in each evaluation site, prompts shaped on instruction types, one embodiment. Not transfer (EVIDENCE rule 2).
assessment.author_claim_kept: LM-Nav composes large pretrained language, vision and navigation models without target-environment finetuning or language-labelled navigation data, allowing a mobile robot to follow free-form textual instructions over long distances in novel outdoor settings. Narrative: 85% of experiments followed without collisions or disengagements.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On 20 author-designed landmark instructions in two outdoor sites mapped beforehand by manual driving, a Jackal robot using frozen GPT-3, CLIP and ViNG with graph search reached net success 16/20 (planning 17/20) with one intervention over ~6.4 km; the reachability-aware objective and the learned navigation model are load-bearing in ablations. Verbs and non-landmark constraints are not followed.
assessment.reproduction: Author-reported only; nothing run by us.

G.reason: Clear sourced gap (annotation-heavy instruction following vs language-free self-supervised navigation) with named neighbours (VLN, SayCan, Huang et al.), but no quantitative comparison to them; residue stated (landmark-only, platform-specific VNM, pre-explored map). Both seats agree.

M.reason: The explicit objective (CLIP landmark likelihood x discounted VNM traversability) solved by dynamic programming makes a distinguishable prediction confirmed by the max-likelihood and GPS ablations. But the central claim is following free-form instructions, while the method reduces an instruction to an ordered landmark list and discards verbs/constraints (authors' main limitation), and the per-node softmax assumes every landmark is present. That load-bearing reduction limits problem-fit below the M=4 anchor.

X.reason: Pipeline, prompts, graph-building rules and search algorithm are given; information access clear (no overhead imagery, map from manual traversal). Exact reconstruction limited by unspecified gamma/alpha, the <2 s vs 1 s temporal threshold conflict and 'three' vs two displayed prompt examples. Both seats agree.

measurement.reason: Real traversals with disengagement counts and route efficiency, but net-success criterion is not defined (only planning success is), planning success is judged against an 'intended path' by an unstated rater, each query runs once, and the narrative 85% differs from Table 1 net success. Anchors v2 cap at 2. Both seats agree.

causality.reason: One-at-a-time ablations: VNM removed (robot runs, EnvSmall only), search objective (planning, both environments), LLM and VLM swaps (component benchmarks). LLM test uses the 20 evaluation prompts; VLM metric is a permissive top-3; no alternative-paradigm baseline on the same routes. Both seats agree.

holdout.reason: Frozen weights meet new sites, but the topological graph (harness memory) is built by manually driving each evaluation environment, VLM test landmarks partly come from the evaluation instructions, the prompt was shaped on instruction types, one robot. Both seats agree.

statistics.reason: Ten single runs per environment, no variance or CI; failure attribution only qualitative and partly inconsistent with Table 1. Anchors v2: no repetition and no failure decomposition -> <=1. Both seats agree.

cost.reason: No compute/API/latency figures and the per-site manual mapping drive is not quantified; but physical operating cost is measured: route efficiency (described vs executed length) and human interventions per run. Partial cost-relevant measurement keeps it above not_reported; no budget matching across ablations.
